set_aside.subject: schema creation owner and invocation
set_aside.text: “module:portal_store … creates every repository schema when a transaction begins” and “module:portal_store owns … schema creation through the repositories” conflict with “the sqlite unit-of-work backend lowers PortalStore.begin with them … so no generated module calls them.”
set_aside.question: Does the generated portal_store implementation call the ten repository schema capabilities, or does a non-module backend perform schema creation without those module calls—and, in the latter case, who owns that runtime step?
options: PortalStore imports and calls each repository schema capability in the listed order.
A generated backend hook outside all modules calls the repository schema capabilities.
The backend performs equivalent schema SQL directly, without calling repository capabilities.
set_aside.default_guess: Generate the calls inside module:portal_store, because State 3 assigns it the connection, transaction, repository wiring, and schema-creation responsibility.

witness.initial: A configured service starts with a new SQLite database containing none of the ten schemas.
events: A readiness request makes module:runtime begin a PortalStore transaction.
The changed flow requires all ten schemas to be created before the transaction is returned.
outcomes: The generated portal_store module invokes each repository's create_*_schema capability in the listed order.
No generated module invokes those capabilities; an unnamed backend hook or direct backend SQL creates the schemas.
witness.observer: A code generator, module-dependency checker, or test instrumenting the repository schema capabilities sees the difference.

set_aside.subject: unit-of-work backend rule identity
set_aside.text: The change cites “rules.sqlite_unit_of_work_backend” and schema “create_on_begin_in_accessor_order”, while the accepted texts define portal_store against “rules.persistence_backend” and carry only “rules.persistence_backend” to the persistence closure; no relationship between these rule addresses is stated.
set_aside.question: Is rules.sqlite_unit_of_work_backend a rename or child of rules.persistence_backend, or is it a new backend rule that later states must define?
options: It is the same backend as rules.persistence_backend under a new name.
It is a named subsection of rules.persistence_backend.
It is a separate rule that must coexist with rules.persistence_backend.
set_aside.default_guess: Treat create_on_begin_in_accessor_order as part of the existing rules.persistence_backend, since that is the backend State 3 assigns to portal_store.

witness.initial: Later assembly contains the previously declared rules.persistence_backend but no declared rules.sqlite_unit_of_work_backend.
events: It resolves the changed flow's lowering address to determine how schemas are created.
outcomes: The implementer treats the new address as an alias/subsection and generates schema creation from rules.persistence_backend.
The implementer treats it as a distinct required rule and either invents its contents or cannot generate PortalStore.begin.
witness.observer: The State 6/7 author or code generator sees a different rule graph and potentially different generated begin implementation.
